name: Computer Physics
overview: The first two years pair mathematical analysis, algebra, mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum and statistical physics with programming, algorithms, Unix, object-oriented programming and numerical methods. Teaching mixes lectures, problem-solving classes, laboratories and workshops, and you are assessed through exams and projects. Electives let you lean towards artificial intelligence and machine learning, data science, GPU computing, digital systems or scientific computing. Graduates go into research institutes, engineering firms, high-performance computing centres and industrial R&D, or on to a master's in a physics-related field such as Technical Physics.

name: Computer Science
overview: The first year builds the mathematical base (analysis, algebra, discrete mathematics, logic, statistics) alongside introductory computer science, Unix, two programming courses and physics. Lectures are joined by laboratory and project classes, and later years add elective groups such as semantic web, process mining, programming language theory, constraint and logic programming. The course includes a required internship in semester 6 and a capstone project in semester 7, and a business analysis information systems option is available. It prepares engineers for software development, systems administration, data analysis and the design of PC and mobile systems.

name: Computer Science for Embedded Systems
overview: You start with algebra, mathematical analysis, programming, operating systems administration, data transmission, microcontroller basics and digital electronics, then move on to algorithms, object-oriented and functional programming, physics and metrology. Classes combine lectures, laboratories, workshops and project work. Instead of fixed tracks, electives in the later years cover low-level and high-level programming, real-time operating systems, FPGA and GPU acceleration, system security, signal processing, embedded AI and wireless systems. Graduates work on embedded design in sectors such as automotive, robotics, IoT and medical devices, or continue to a second-cycle degree.

name: Geology of Natural Resources
overview: The first year covers mathematics for geologists, chemistry, physical geology, mineralogy and petrology, physics in geology, statistics and geostatistics, GIS, environmental assessment and computational geoscience. Fieldwork is a large part of the course, with 90 hours of field courses in year one and 60 in year two, plus lab classes, projects, an internship and a seminar leading to a diploma project. In the final years you choose pathways such as geoenergy resources, mining hydrogeology, geomaterials, remote sensing, renewables and the energy transition, or computational deposit analysis. Graduates enter the raw materials industry, mineral exploration, mining companies, research, consultancy and public administration.

name: Mechanical Engineering
overview: Year one lays the groundwork with mathematics, physics, chemistry, information technology, manufacturing processes, engineering drawing, fundamentals of mechanical engineering and materials science. Teaching combines lectures, laboratories, seminars and project classes where you learn design and CAD, and a practical placement comes in the final year. For the diploma you choose one of nine profiles, for example ropeway transport systems, earthmoving and heavy-duty machinery, energy technologies, manufacturing process engineering, advanced design methods or ecological systems engineering. Graduates design mechanical systems, and the programme reports that most find work within months, at firms such as Valeo, Delphi and ABB.

name: Mechatronic Engineering
overview: The first year covers algebra, analysis, physics, chemistry, programming and the basics of informatics, followed in year two by mechanics, strength of materials, engineering drawing, signals and systems, numerical methods, manufacturing technology, and electronics and electrical engineering. Lectures are combined with auditorium, laboratory and project classes and seminars. Later optional modules let you focus on robotics (industrial or service robots), intelligent methods such as deep learning or vision, signal processing, and object-oriented or microcontroller programming. Graduates work in design offices, R&D institutions and companies that make or use mechatronic devices, or continue to a master's in Poland or abroad.

name: Space Engineering
overview: The opening year combines calculus, algebra, physics, engineering mechanics, materials science and chemistry with programming, electronics, engineering design and CAD. The emphasis is hands-on: laboratories, design studios, system integration workshops and multi-stage engineering projects modelled on real missions, plus an obligatory industry or research internship. Electives in later years cover spacecraft subsystems (avionics, power and thermal, propulsion), space systems engineering, Earth observation, space robotics and rovers, mission cybersecurity, space economy and policy, and bioastronautics. Graduates move into spacecraft and satellite engineering, mission operations, avionics and control, space software and data engineering, or on to a master's in a space-related field.

name: Chemistry
overview: The degree has a general academic profile and builds a broad grounding in analytical, inorganic, organic and physical chemistry, with further study of chemical technology, instrumental analysis, spectral methods and crystallochemistry. Specialisation is in general chemistry rather than a narrow branch. Graduates find work in the chemical industry, in chemical and analytical laboratories, in quality control, in research centres, in product development and in companies supplying equipment and reagents.

name: European Legal Studies
overview: Compulsory courses include introduction to international law, philosophy of law, the European Convention on Human Rights, international protection of human rights, freedom of speech and its limits, free movement and migration policy in the EU, EU trade and consumer law, intellectual property, judicial cooperation in civil and criminal matters, private international law and data protection. In the third year you choose a focus track on issues in law, business and society, and electives range from EU criminal law and food law to sectoral energy and telecommunications law and European identity. Graduates apply European law knowledge in public bodies, economic institutions and private business, including in their home countries.

name: Central European and Balkan Studies
overview: The programme rests on three modules: Polish language education, Slavistics and classical philology, topped up with skills in intercultural communication for tourism and business. It is aimed at people who want to work with the cultures and languages of Central Europe and the Balkans. Graduates can work in European cultural institutions such as museums, community centres, publishers and theatres, in radio, television and online media, in marketing and advertising, and in tourism, airlines and hotels.

name: English Linguistics: Theories, Interfaces, Technologies
overview: Study is organised in four areas: theoretical linguistics (phonology, syntax, psycholinguistics, sociolinguistics, language acquisition, cognitive linguistics), interdisciplinary linguistics with research methods, experimental work and field studies, language technology such as text processing, building language databases and speech analysis, and academic English covering pronunciation, discourse, grammar and public speaking. Training includes placements in companies. Graduates go into firms working with language data and language technologies, editorial and media work, PR, advertising, translation, education, market and opinion research, and journalism.

name: International Relations
overview: Alongside comparative politics, the programme looks at intercultural communication, political campaigns, media and international communication, stereotypes in international relations, contentious politics, charismatic leadership and leadership in international business. Lectures are combined with workshops, exercises and internships, in classes built around discussion with experienced staff. Graduates are prepared for diplomatic and consular offices, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other public institutions, as well as international companies.

name: Liberal Arts and Sciences
overview: Core courses in philosophy, research methodology, logic and academic writing run alongside English throughout the three years, with the chance to take ancient Greek and Latin. Disciplinary courses draw on biology, physics, geography, political science and history, and from the second year you choose one course from this programme and two from other university faculties. The programme is part of the European Consortium of Liberal Arts and Sciences. Graduates are described as having analytical and communication skills useful in business, academia, government and the nonprofit sector, and many go on to study medicine, law or education.

name: Global Communication
overview: The programme covers linguistics, literary studies, culture and communication studies, with language training in English, Russian and a third language of your choice: Spanish, German, Belarusian or Ukrainian. Alongside lectures there are exercises, conversation classes, laboratories and workshops. Graduates work in international organisations and public administration, NGOs and foundations, cultural institutions, international firms, marketing and publishing, and in logistics or customer service roles for companies serving Central and Eastern European markets. A second-cycle degree is open to those continuing in fields that need English, Russian and another foreign language.

name: Applied Linguistics and Intercultural Communication
overview: English and German are studied together, with descriptive grammar of each, contrastive grammar of the two languages, introductory linguistics and text and discourse linguistics. A cultural-communication strand covers public speaking, intercultural competence training and multilingualism and multiculturalism in the European Union. You also take a third language, Spanish or French. Graduates work in international and multicultural organisations, public relations, advertising and creative agencies, translation offices and travel agencies.

name: Governance of Organizations
overview: The curriculum draws on three areas: political science and administration, law, and communication and media. Project work and soft-skills classes build abilities such as conflict management, argumentation and public speaking, including the use of AI, and an intensive foreign-language course, preferably German, is included. You also learn about ESG, compliance management and political and business communication. Graduates can work in government agencies, administrative bodies and EU institutions, or in businesses, foundations, associations and NGOs, and the degree leads on to master's courses in Poland and abroad.

name: Bachelor in Management
overview: Six semesters cover management fundamentals, finance, accounting, human resource management, micro- and macroeconomics, marketing, organisational studies, entrepreneurship, corporate law and strategic management. You build business plans, run marketing research projects and play management business games, visit company headquarters, and complete a mandatory three-week internship in the final semester. The fifth semester is a mobility window for exchange at partner universities. You choose a major: Sustainable Business with ESCP Business School, Entrepreneurship, Marketing, International Management or Luxury Management, with double-degree options at KEDGE, Limerick, PUCPR and MBS. Graduates become managers in multinational firms, marketing specialists, entrepreneurs and international project leaders.

name: Sustainable Business - Major on the Bachelor in Management Program
overview: Courses centre on ESG frameworks, green economics and sustainable competitiveness, sustainable business models, impact and regenerative entrepreneurship, CSR and business ethics, and business strategy with sustainability. Learning is practical, through business games, group projects, diploma workshops and an internship of at least three weeks after the third semester. You spend the first year in Warsaw and then move to an ESCP Business School campus in Turin, Madrid, Paris, Berlin or London for years two and three, earning a double degree. Graduates aim for roles such as sustainability consultant, CSR manager, environmental manager, sustainable supply chain manager or policy advisor in business, the public sector and NGOs.

name: Bachelor in Management and Artificial Intelligence
overview: AI and data courses (Python and machine learning, big data and algorithms, statistics for machine learning, cloud infrastructures, data visualisation, generative AI for managers) sit beside management subjects such as innovation, project and strategic management, digital marketing, finance, law and economics. From the second semester you work in groups on startup-style projects, with hands-on input from industry partners including Oracle Academy, the Polish Academy of Sciences, EY and Roche, and you can earn programming certificates. High-achieving students can pursue a double degree with LUISS in Italy. Graduates become data analysts, IT consultants and digital transformation specialists, or managers in banking, insurance, telecoms, public administration and startups.

name: Bachelor in Management and Sociology in Business and Media
overview: The course mixes management and economics with media sociology: marketing, entrepreneurship and business planning, traditional and new media, social research methods, internet marketing and e-business, design thinking and service design, big data, digital PR, media economics and AI in business and media. Classes are workshops and discussions that use professional media studios and computer labs, with some sessions in virtual reality. Electives let you choose between human capital management and organisational well-being, then media monitoring or data mining, and partners include Gemius, CANAL+ Polska, Newspoint and Voice House. Graduates work in advertising and PR agencies, internet marketing, consulting, traditional and digital media, research centres and e-commerce.

name: Bachelor in Finance and Accounting
overview: You study financial accounting, microeconomics, management principles, corporate finance, financial markets, sustainable finance and professional financial terminology. Practical elements include a mandatory internship, training on financial databases in the Bloomberg Finance Lab, business simulations, guest lectures from senior managers, and a semester-five window for international exchange. You choose among three majors: Corporate Finance and Financial Markets, Green Finance, or FinTech and Digital Transformation in Finance. Graduates work in finance departments of international companies and financial institutions, in sustainable finance, consulting or entrepreneurship, and can continue to the university's master's in finance and accounting or to double degrees at ISEG Lisbon, Aston or IESEG.

name: Master of Pharmacy
overview: The five-year programme looks at the science behind drug discovery, development and delivery, and at how patients respond to the medicines they take. Training includes six months of pre-registration practice in an approved pharmacy. The degree leads to registration as a pharmacist in Poland, which is recognised in other EU member states.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
overview: Over three years the curriculum combines basic sciences (anatomy, physiology, pathology, genetics, biochemistry, microbiology, pharmacology, radiology) with social sciences such as psychology, sociology, medical law, public health and nursing ethics. Nursing care itself is taught through health promotion, primary care, dietetics, physical examination and nursing research, then specialist areas including internal medicine, paediatrics, surgery, midwifery, psychiatry, anaesthesiology, geriatrics, palliative care and emergency medicine. Practical classes and professional placements are part of the course. Graduates can obtain a professional qualification certificate from the District Chamber of Nurses and Midwives in Poland.

name: Doctor of Medicine
overview: This is a single six-year master's-level course in medicine taught in English, which begins with an orientation week. Study includes practical classes and professional placements alongside the theoretical teaching.

name: Medicine
overview: The course leads to the Doctor of Medicine degree and combines clinical training, laboratory work and practice in a medical simulation centre, with practical training and electives built into the curriculum. Exams follow the NBME format, and a Kaplan Step 1 preparation course is offered. The university's clinical hospital serves as a teaching base. Graduates can follow routes to medical licensing in many countries, with guidance on residency placement and a postgraduate internship in English.

name: Dentistry
overview: This five-year course leads school leavers to the professional Doctor of Dental Surgery degree. Teaching is built around hands-on work with patients, a medical simulation centre and a practical summer training placement, with basic science and clinical evaluations along the way. The degree opens routes to dental licensing in Europe and elsewhere, supported by guidance on national licensing and the legalisation of diplomas.

name: Architecture
overview: The curriculum spans architectural, urban, landscape and interior design, building construction, structural systems, building physics, materials, geotechnics, building law, project management, architectural history, art theory and heritage conservation. Studio design projects form the core, with lectures, workshops, competitions, two-week field internships in inventory work, urban planning and drawing, and a full seventh semester in an architectural office. The faculty highlights healthcare design, sustainable and energy-efficient building and heritage protection, and takes part in Erasmus+ exchange. Graduates work as assistants in architectural and planning offices, interior architects, set designers, computer graphics designers, or in local government administration.

name: Artificial Intelligence
overview: The seven-semester course covers algorithmics, machine learning and neural networks, data analysis and exploration, information acquisition and processing, optimisation and decision analysis, and AI in robotics. Learning takes place in laboratories and projects, with a four-week professional internship after the third year and a thesis. Exchange routes run through Erasmus+, EUNICE and IAESTE. Graduates work in IT companies, R&D centres and organisations that use smart technologies, or continue to a master degree and the doctoral school.

name: Automatic Control and Robotics
overview: After a grounding in mathematical analysis, algebra, differential equations and programming, you study circuit theory, signal processing, electronics and digital techniques, control systems, robotics, mechanics, microprocessor systems, PLC programming, real-time systems and system identification. Work happens in well-equipped laboratories and projects, with a mandatory four-week internship in the second year and a diploma project in semester 7. At master level the course branches into intelligent automation, robots and autonomous systems, control systems and visual systems. Graduates find work in industrial production, transport, telecommunications, energy and healthcare.

name: Biomedical Engineering
overview: Over seven semesters you study mathematics, physics, chemistry and computing, engineering basics such as mechanics, materials science and metrology, and the biomedical core of anatomy, biophysics, biomechanics, bioinformatics and biomaterials. Further topics include medical apparatus, imaging techniques, surgical instruments, prosthetics, CAD/CAM, signal processing, robotics and tissue engineering. Teaching uses laboratories, design projects, seminars with medical doctors and physiotherapists, a four-week internship in semester 6 and a supervised thesis. A master degree follows in medical and rehabilitation devices or implant and prosthetics engineering, and graduates design medical devices, implement technology in healthcare or manage medical device products.

name: Chemical Technology
overview: Seven semesters combine general, inorganic, organic, analytical and physical chemistry with chemical engineering, reactor engineering, chemical apparatus, and inorganic, organic and polymer technology, supported by mathematics, physics, thermodynamics, electrochemistry and process control. Teaching is through laboratory and project classes, a six-week professional internship after semester 6, a technological project and a diploma thesis. Master specialisations are composites and nanomaterials, technical electrochemistry, organic technology and polymer technology. Graduates design and supervise technological processes in chemical and petrochemical industries or work in control, diagnostic and research laboratories.

name: Engineering Management
overview: The course joins engineering with business: mathematics, micro- and macroeconomics, management fundamentals, organisational science, human resources, materials science, computer graphics, programming, manufacturing process design, finance, accounting, marketing, quality and project management, and Industry 4.0 IT systems. Teaching includes laboratories, projects, a mandatory four-week internship in semester 6 and a thesis, in facilities equipped with VR. A master degree can be taken in managing future enterprises or in managing enterprise resources and processes. Graduates become market analysts, sales managers, designers of management systems, mid-level managers (especially in production firms) or business founders.

name: Mechanical Engineering
overview: Across seven semesters you cover mathematics, physics, engineering analysis, materials science and metallurgy, manufacturing technologies such as machining, welding and heat treatment, CAD/CAE/CAM, machine construction, mechatronics, automation and robotics, electronics, fluid mechanics and hydraulics, and AI methods in control. Laboratories, project work and teamwork modelled on industrial problems are followed by a four-week internship in semester 6 and a diploma thesis, supported by close faculty ties with industry. A master degree offers mechatronic constructions or automation and production systems supervision. Graduates work as design engineers, technologists, production engineers, quality and maintenance specialists and R&D engineers.

name: Microelectronics and Digital Communication
overview: The programme centres on microelectronics (microcomputers, FPGA circuits, electronic board design), programming for x86, ARM, signal processors and FPGAs, and digital communication including satellite, smartphone, multimedia and quantum communication. Further topics include XR and VR technologies, human-machine interaction, smart device programming and sensor networks. Teaching is based on laboratory work, design and programming projects and a mandatory vocational internship in semester 6, with Erasmus+, EUNICE and IAESTE placements available. Graduates can move into work built on this practical knowledge or continue to a master degree.

name: Quantum Technologies
overview: Quantum physics is combined with classical and quantum computing, AI, photonics, electronics and materials engineering, alongside physics, chemistry, mathematics, electrical engineering, metrology, crystallography, microscopy and materials processing. Materials engineering makes up about half of the curriculum, covering functional materials and nanostructures, thin-film structures for qubit platforms, quantum sensors and quantum communication systems. You work in laboratories and on CAD/CAM projects, complete a four-week internship after semester 6, and prepare a thesis. Graduates go into research and development, process optimisation, medical and other diagnostics, sensing, and quantum hardware and software.

name: Sustainable Building Engineering
overview: Seven semesters cover mathematics, physics and building chemistry, structural, soil and fluid mechanics, building materials and concrete technology, design of masonry, timber, concrete and steel structures, HVAC and water systems, building physics, construction law and surveying. Project work includes architectural design with BIM across three semesters, with a two-week surveying practicum in year one, a two-week geotechnical practicum in year two, a four-week external internship in year three and a thesis. Energy efficiency, lifecycle assessment and lifecycle costing run through the course. Graduates work in construction companies, design offices, R&D centres and infrastructure organisations.

name: Architecture
overview: The curriculum covers design and planning of urban spaces and architectural volumes, architectural and town-planning theory, history of architecture, fine arts techniques, building economics and investment, design process management with BIM, energy efficiency and circular economy solutions. Most teaching happens in the atelier, where you work under a chosen academic teacher, with unified design seminar blocks in the first four semesters and optional workshops and interdisciplinary seminars in semesters 5 to 8. A preparatory course covers fine art techniques and Polish architecture and culture, and the degree ends with a diploma design thesis presented orally. Graduates work as designers, project managers in building investment, representatives of developers and contractors, or land and real estate consultants; architect licensure follows master-level study.

name: Electric and Hybrid Vehicles Engineering
overview: Modules include mechatronic systems design, sensors and actuators, automation, construction and navigation of autonomous vehicles, ultralight vehicle bodies, crashworthiness, vehicle information systems, energy harvesting, ionics and photovoltaics, diagnosis of electric and hybrid vehicles, advanced control of electric and hybrid drives, and vehicle recycling. Classes and laboratories stress practical work with design and IT tools. You learn to model power train components and to design and test simple multi-source energy storage systems. Graduates can work in the automotive industry on electric and hybrid drives, in machinery sectors, and in transport and energy roles focused on green, energy-efficient technology.

name: Environmental Engineering
overview: Coursework is grouped into basic sciences, engineering tools (programming, CAD, numerical methods, operations research, AI and GIS), fundamentals of civil engineering, building services and fluid network design, systems modelling and automatic control, and project and investment management. You develop skills in designing building installations such as HVAC, in designing and managing fluid networks, and in water engineering, environmental technologies, the circular economy and the energy transition. The faculty prepares graduates for construction licences in installation, hydrotechnical and structural engineering, with full qualification after a master degree. Graduates work in water, wastewater, gas and heating infrastructure companies, environmental technology firms, design and consulting offices and technical auditing.

name: Environmental Protection
overview: The curriculum is organised in modules on basic sciences, engineering tools (programming, CAD, numerical methods, GIS), law and economics in environmental protection, climate change and air pollution, land surface protection, hydrology and water management, environmental hazards, municipal services and sustainable cities. Specialist strands cover climate neutrality, environmental measurement techniques, and biotechnology with sustainable development. More than 60 percent of classes are practical, including a project-based learning module. Graduates work in environmental consulting and impact assessment, company environmental departments, local and national administration, municipal utilities, planning bodies, site remediation firms and engineering companies.

name: Civil Engineering
overview: You start with mathematics, physics, mechanics and chemistry, add social sciences and humanities, and move into the core civil engineering areas of structures, surveying, transportation, materials science, management and environment. After year three you choose a specialisation: civil engineering structures, construction engineering and management, energy-saving construction or transportation engineering, with electives such as reinforced concrete and steel structures, renewable energy sources, energy efficiency and cost estimation. An integrated project is available. Graduates take part in the planning, design, construction, operation and maintenance of civil engineering facilities.

name: Electrical Engineering
overview: The programme covers electrical materials technology, electrical measurements, circuits and systems, the electromagnetic field, electrical machines, electrical power engineering, converter drive control, high voltage technology and IT. Specific modules include CAD methods, electronics, numerical methods, microprocessor engineering, instrumentation and signal transmission, and electric traction. You then follow one of two specialisations: Control and Computer Engineering, or Electrical Power Engineering.

name: Computer Science
overview: The first two years are shared with the telecommunications programme and form a common grounding in information and communications technology. Modules include algorithms and programming, circuits and systems, computer systems, telecommunications, operating systems, graphical user interfaces, databases, cryptography and information security, software engineering, compiling techniques and an introduction to artificial intelligence. You work with object programming, CASE-tool-aided design, system analysis, modelling and prototyping, and specialise in computer systems and networks. The aim is to design, implement and operate complex computer systems and networks independently.

name: Computer Science and Information Systems
overview: The first three semesters lay a mathematical base, and all students share core courses through semester four: programming in C, C++, Java and C#/.NET, discrete mathematics, algorithms, data structures, operating systems, databases, networks, software engineering, AI, numerical methods, embedded systems and computer graphics. From semester five you choose electives with theoretical and practical emphasis, and the seventh semester is largely given over to team projects and the thesis. Teaching combines lectures, seminars, programming laboratories, team projects and individual thesis work. Graduates can work on IT projects, system verification, and the administration of medium-scale information systems and networks.

name: Mechatronics
overview: The programme covers Matlab programming, 3D CAD, mechatronic drives, theory of machines and mechanisms, microcontrollers, sensors and measuring devices, design of electronic modules, multimedia devices, MEMS and electric metrology. The focus is on practical knowledge of computer design, microprocessor control, drives and actuators, applied to drive systems, measurement devices and automation of manufacturing. Graduates can work in electromechanical and automotive industries, household appliance and machine tool manufacturing, aviation and plants that operate mechatronic systems, or go on to a master degree.

name: Aerospace Engineering
overview: The first year builds foundational sciences, the second turns to mechanical design and control engineering, and the third focuses on aerospace topics such as introduction to aerospace, materials in aerospace technology, mechanics of flight, aircraft engine design, aircraft design, aeronautical systems, risk and reliability in aviation and rotorcraft aeromechanics. Design work uses integrated CAD/CAM/CAE systems, and the last half-year is supervised work on the engineering thesis. You choose between two specialisations: Aerospace Propulsion Systems, and Aerospace Structures and Systems. Graduates are prepared for the aerospace industry, airlines, other industries and research institutions working on aircraft and spacecraft.

name: Power Engineering
overview: The first year covers mathematics, physics, mechanics, thermodynamics and computer science, the second adds mechanical design fundamentals and control engineering, and years two and three specialise in thermodynamics and fluid mechanics, heat transfer, electric machines and electronics, combustion and fuels, flow machines, electric power systems, thermal power systems, renewable energy and environmental protection technology. Laboratory work includes measurement and experiment technique, and the final half-year is supervised work on the engineering thesis. Graduates are prepared for industry roles in designing, commissioning and operating power systems, covering energy production, conversion, transmission and distribution.

name: Global Business, Finance and Governance
overview: The course blends economics, finance, management, international business, marketing and international trade with training in data collection and analysis, and teaching includes projects and research tasks. You choose one of four tracks: European Economic Integration Towards Global Challenges (EU institutions and policy), Global Development and Governance (sustainable development and international organisations), International Business, or International Finance (capital markets, exchange rates, financial risk). Double degrees are possible with partners in China, Germany and South Korea. Graduates start in finance, sales, logistics and marketing roles in companies, NGOs, government agencies and international organisations, or continue to a master's or doctorate at SGH.

name: International Economics
overview: The first three semesters cover micro- and macroeconomics, management and accounting, finance, economic and social policy, European integration, statistics and two foreign languages. The last three follow an economics, business or politics and law track, with courses such as international competitiveness, international finance, corporate finance, international marketing, international organisations and public international law. You can add a minor in Digital World Economy, Economics of EU membership or International Entrepreneurship, and double degrees are offered with Peking University, Pforzheim, Kyungpook National University and Kyiv National Economic University. Graduates go into international companies, EU administration, international organisations such as the OECD, IMF and UN, research institutes, media or their own business.

name: Management
overview: The course teaches how organisations operate, with management sciences and economics, the basic functions of planning, organising, motivating, monitoring and coordinating, and the formulation, planning and control of projects. Learning is practical, through project work, the student internship programme and exchange options. You specialise in Entrepreneurship, Marketing or Project Management, and double degrees are available with Peking University (Guanghua School of Management) and European University Viadrina. Graduates become specialists or middle managers in businesses, non-profits and public administration, start their own firms, or move on to a master's degree.

name: Quantitative Methods in Economics and Information Systems
overview: You study mathematical analysis and linear algebra, probability and mathematical statistics, research design, demography, mathematical economics, econometrics, operational research, finance and insurance mathematics, programming, information systems design and databases. Laboratory classes in small groups put modern tools to use on real examples and empirical analysis. You choose between two specialisations: Econometrics, for building and interpreting models in economics, finance and social sciences, or Methods of Decision Analysis, with risk assessment and data analysis. Graduates work in organisations that apply mathematical, statistical, econometric and information tools, start their own business, or go on to a master's degree; exchange, double degree and Erasmus+ options exist.

name: Psychology
overview: The core covers social psychology, the biological foundations of behaviour, emotion and motivation, developmental, personality and cognitive psychology, psychopathology, individual differences and psychometrics. Teaching links theory to practice through at least one project-based course each year, practical internships, practicum placements and thesis seminars. A Global-MINDS specialisation in cross-cultural psychology is available, and students come into contact with research centres on decision making, the biological basis of social behaviour and social and technological innovation. Graduates work as psychotherapists, researchers, developmental, business, market research or sports psychologists and human-computer interaction specialists, or continue to a master's in Clinical Psychology or Applied Social Psychology.

name: Psychology
overview: You study social psychology, the biological foundations of behaviour, emotion and motivation, developmental, personality and cognitive psychology, psychopathology, individual differences and psychometrics, with attention to cognition, social dynamics and cultural influences. The course links theory and practice, with at least one project-based course each year for solving real problems or doing group research, alongside training in professional interpersonal skills. Clinical and health psychology are among the areas you can focus on. Graduates work as psychotherapists, researchers, developmental, business, market research or sports psychologists and human-computer interaction specialists, and master's options include Applied Social Psychology and Clinical Psychology.

name: Psychology
overview: Study begins with social psychology, the biological foundations of behaviour, emotion and motivation, developmental, personality and cognitive psychology, psychopathology, individual differences and psychometrics, and extends to social and cultural dynamics and applications in education, work and healthcare. Hands-on skills are developed in professional laboratories for behavioural research under the supervision of lecturers. The curriculum touches social, clinical and health, economic, criminal and environmental psychology. Graduates work as psychotherapists, researchers, developmental, occupational, market research or sports psychologists and HCI specialists, and the degree prepares for master's study in clinical or applied social psychology.

name: Psychology
overview: The core subjects are social psychology, biological foundations of behaviour, emotion and motivation, developmental, personality and cognitive psychology, psychopathology, individual differences and psychometrics. Classes bring theory into real-world scenarios, with at least one project-based course each year for problem solving and group research. The programme touches clinical and health, organisational and educational psychology. Graduates work as psychotherapists, researchers, developmental psychologists, human-computer interaction specialists, business and occupational psychologists, market researchers, sports psychologists and health and wellness professionals.

name: Computer Science
overview: You study logic, linear algebra, analysis, probability and statistics, programming in Python, Java, JavaScript and C, algorithms, data structures, discrete mathematics, operating systems, computer architecture, networks, cloud computing, databases, cybersecurity, cryptography and machine learning, plus soft skills and entrepreneurship. Teaching combines lectures and practicals in well-equipped computer labs, individual and team projects, workshops, a graduation thesis and 780 hours of internships with partner companies such as Nethone, Schneider Electric Polska and Wolters Kluwer Polska. From semester five you choose between Cybersecurity and Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning. Graduates work as software developers, data scientists, cloud administrators, cybersecurity specialists, machine learning engineers and IT project managers.

name: Design
overview: The first years build foundations in 2D and 3D design, visual and colour analysis, photography, graphic design, parametric design, philosophy, psychology, art anthropology and fashion history. Learning is studio-based in workshops for ceramics, metalwork, woodwork, sewing, screen printing and digital fabrication, with projects across specialisations carried out with business and community partners. In year two you choose Message (communication design), Object (product design) or Space (spatial design), and in the fourth year you complete a graduation project with design and written parts, supervised by two staff members.

name: English Studies
overview: The core combines practical English and grammar, pronunciation, phonetics and phonology, academic writing, American and British literature and civilisation, with linguistics and critical thinking. Training includes tools for computer-assisted translation, a simultaneous interpretation lab for the translation track and teaching internships on the TEFL track. You pick a track: Teaching English as a Foreign Language, English Studies for Media and Creative Industries, English Studies for Business Environment, or Translation Studies (Polish and English). Graduates work as teachers, translators, interpreters, corporate specialists, journalists, PR professionals, diplomats and in tourism.

name: English Studies with Additional Language
overview: Practical English and grammar, pronunciation, phonetics and phonology, academic writing and American and British literature and civilisation are taught alongside 540 hours of a second language chosen from Chinese, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean and Spanish. Classes include reading seminars, computer-assisted translation practice, an interpretation lab for the translation track and teaching internships for future English teachers. In the second year you choose a track: teaching English as a foreign language, media and creative industries, business environment, or Polish-English translation following EU guidelines. Graduates work as teachers, translators, interpreters, translation managers, journalists, PR professionals, diplomatic staff and tourism specialists.

name: Management and Leadership
overview: You learn management methods and tools, self-management, collaboration and communication, setting up and funding a business, social innovation, evidence-based management, traditional and agile project management, leadership and organisational culture, sales, finance, change management and data analysis. Teaching is experiential, with real projects commissioned by business partners, business simulations, case studies and 960 hours of internships over the three years; partners include mBank, Nordea, DHL, Procter and Gamble and Volkswagen Poznan. After year one you choose between Start-ups and Project Management. Graduates work as project managers, start-up founders, business developers, product owners, business analysts, innovation specialists and agile coaches.

name: Earth Sciences in a Changing World
overview: The three-year course gives a grounding in geography, geology and the ways human activity transforms the environment. Classes use the faculty's specialised research laboratories and analytical equipment, plus field activities in Poland and abroad. It was developed with European Social Fund Plus funding. Graduates can identify and describe human-driven environmental change, assess its natural, social and economic effects, and apply environmental management and sustainable development methods, with second-cycle and post-diploma study as next steps.

name: East European Studies: Languages and Discourses
overview: Compulsory courses cover the history of Eastern Europe, basic linguistics, discourse studies and memory studies, together with two Slavic languages chosen from Russian, Ukrainian and Polish, and a broad choice of optional courses. Teaching is entirely in English in small groups, and companies that cooperate with the faculty offer internships. Graduates work in international, governmental and non-governmental organisations, local government, cultural institutions, business, journalism and diplomacy, or continue to a second-cycle degree or the Doctoral School in the Humanities.

name: European Studies
overview: The interdisciplinary core looks at European politics, culture and society through comparative politics, EU governance, human rights law, social change and protest movements, gender politics, digitalisation and environmental movements. Over three years you choose between two specialisations: Governing Europe and Central Eastern European Politics, covering political systems, post-1989 transformations, illiberalism and populism, or Social Change in Europe, covering digitalisation, environmental movements, migration and technological disruption. Language options include Polish, Russian, German and French. Graduates work in public administration, EU and national institutions, NGOs, cultural institutions and media, and the degree leads on to graduate study.

name: Global and Development Studies
overview: The programme brings together law, politics, economics, history, social relations, culture and communication to study globalisation and international development. You can focus on a particular part of the world or on specific global problems. The faculty runs courses under agreements with foreign universities and takes part in Erasmus+, CEEPUS, the Utrecht Network and Una Europa exchanges. Graduates are prepared for public administration, international organisations, NGOs, international companies, cultural institutions, media and publishing, or for master's study such as International Security and Development.

name: International Relations and Area Studies
overview: Subjects include international politics and economics, development and global governance, the ethics of international affairs, conflict resolution and peace building, regional integration, and cultural diversity and intercultural dialogue. You specialise in either International Security or Area Studies. The faculty has agreements with foreign universities and takes part in Erasmus+, CEEPUS, the Utrecht Network and Una Europa. Graduates work in government, NGOs, aid and development agencies, business, diplomacy and cultural or regional institutions, or apply for master's programmes in various social sciences.

name: Mathematics and Computer Science Advanced Track
overview: Mathematics and computer science are studied with an emphasis on theory and research skills, and you have a high degree of freedom in choosing courses. Tutorial-style teaching gives you an individual academic supervisor from the first semester, and you can work on research projects and write scientific papers under a tutor from the first year, alongside laboratory classes in computer labs. Graduates are prepared for research at an international level, going into doctoral programmes, research and development projects or master's study.

name: Responsible Entrepreneurship and Management
overview: The curriculum centres on management and quality sciences, with entrepreneurship and start-up culture, digital transformation and data-driven innovation, how organisations work in international settings, and the principles of sustainable development. Courses come in coherent modules, the faculty works with the business sector, and double degrees with European universities are possible. Graduates become managers, consultants, digital project leaders and founders of ventures in the private, public and non-profit sectors, or continue to second-cycle study.

name: Joint Bachelor in Sustainability
overview: This Una Europa degree starts with introductory and transversal courses in Krakow in the first year, covering the physical basis of climate change, the sustainable development goals, the circular economy and the ethics of sustainability, with language and communication training. In years two and three you choose one of six tracks, each led by a partner university: Sustainable Chemistry and Physics (Helsinki), Economy and Geography (Paris 1 Pantheon-Sorbonne), Law and Politics of Sustainability (Jagiellonian), Environmental and Life Sciences (Complutense Madrid), Economics, Management and Engineering (KU Leuven) and Social Sciences and Humanities (Zurich). An optional final-semester mobility is possible at eight associated universities, and graduates aim for roles such as sustainability consultant, compliance officer or chief sustainability officer.

name: Medicine, Program in English
overview: The first part covers pre-clinical basic sciences, including a medical Polish course so you can talk with patients, and the second part is clinical, so that by the end of year six you have met all clinical specialties. Teaching combines lectures, laboratory classes, clinical training and placements in health care institutions, and problem-based learning from the second year, with visiting professors from the USA, Canada and Germany. Graduates work in health care, education and research, mostly in Norway, Canada, the UK and the US, and can continue in the Doctoral School in Medical and Health Sciences.

name: Dentistry, Program in English
overview: Over five years you study basic sciences and clinical dental disciplines, taught entirely in English with information technology. Practical experience comes through the University Dental Clinic, with both theoretical and hands-on dental care, and the faculty includes visiting professors from the USA, Canada and Germany. Graduates work in public and private health care, education and research, and in private dental practice once suitably qualified, and can continue to the Doctoral School in Medical and Health Sciences.

name: American Studies
overview: Three disciplines are combined: cultural and religious studies as the lead, literary studies, and political and administrative sciences, applied to the culture, literature, arts, film, media, history, economy, politics and law of the United States and the wider Western Hemisphere. Compulsory courses introduce five main disciplines, electives let you build specialist knowledge, and you receive training in research methods and academic writing in English. There are no external internships, but top students can apply for grants for research trips to libraries in Europe and the US. You can spend up to two semesters at another European university through Erasmus+, and a bilateral agreement offers semester stipends at the University of Florida. Graduates work in business, journalism, media, cultural institutions, higher education, public administration, diplomacy and tourism.

name: Archaeology
overview: You study the ancient Mediterranean and South American cultures, excavation methodology and site documentation, data acquisition and processing, museology, and the reading and recording of stratigraphy. Fieldwork is central: seasonal field surveys, at least three excavation seasons, and practical training in documentation and artefact handling, on faculty-led digs in places such as Egypt, Georgia, Armenia, Uzbekistan, Bulgaria, Italy and South America. The final year brings a BA seminar and bachelor's thesis. Graduates can take part in excavations, do archive research, prepare museum catalogues and exhibitions, and continue to second-cycle archaeology studies.

name: Business and Management
overview: Management and quality sciences lead the course, supported by economics and finance, legal sciences, the operational, marketing, financial and personnel functions of an organisation, and research methodology. Teaching relies on individual and team analyses of organisational problems, oral presentations, written assignments, and data analysis and decision-making exercises set in real organisations. Graduates work in industrial and service companies, state and local government and non-profits, starting as analysts or specialists and moving towards middle management, with master's and postgraduate study supporting progression.

name: English Studies
overview: Two paths run from a shared first year: Literature and Culture, covering the literature, history and culture of Anglophone countries plus film studies, ecocriticism, animal studies and media studies, and Linguistics, covering language and the brain, language varieties, language in AI systems and translation studies. Each path offers a minor in a complementary field. All teaching is in English, with practical English classes, project work and research methodology, and you build your own curriculum from the wide range of courses. Graduates can go on to teacher training for English or enter jobs that value the language and soft skills they develop.

name: European Politics and Economics
overview: Run jointly by the faculties of political science and economics, the programme looks at European integration through EU institutions and competences, international economics, trade, currency and economic integration, the internal market, EU law and the successive stages of integration. Teaching is workshop-style, with seminars, simulations of EU institutions, Oxford-style debates and round tables, and analysis of trade databases. Graduates are prepared for public administration, EU institutions and international organisations, business and lobbying firms, NGOs, and media and cultural institutions.

name: Finance, International Investment and Accounting
overview: Courses cover the open economy and international trade, macroeconomic policy under globalisation, international financial management, global banking and financial engineering, foreign asset investment and currency risk, and company valuation across borders. You model economic and social phenomena with mathematical, statistical and econometric tools, working in STATA, Excel and Maxima, and the programme is ACCA-accredited, giving exemptions from professional exams. Graduates go into international banks and financial institutions, strategy and investment consultancies, international organisations, government agencies and global corporations, or on to a master's degree.

name: International Studies in Philosophy
overview: Ontology and epistemology form the base, followed by the history of European and analytical philosophy including the Lvov-Warsaw School, ethics, aesthetics, logic, philosophy of language, philosophical anthropology, social and political philosophy, philosophy of culture, action and mind, and legal philosophy. Lectures supply knowledge, while tutorials and seminars train you to take part in philosophical debate and tackle hard theoretical problems. The three years end with a bachelor's thesis and exam, and the department has a large philosophical library. Graduates work in education, publishing, PR, marketing, mass media and public administration.

name: Psychology
overview: The first three years combine lectures, seminars and exercises on the history of psychology, biological foundations of behaviour, developmental psychology, personality, emotion and motivation, social and clinical psychology, cognitive processes, research methods and statistics, diagnostic methods and professional ethics, with an empirical seminar in year three where you design and carry out your own study. After three years you choose a specialisation: Clinical Psychology (neuropsychology or psychotherapy), Business Psychology, Social Research, or a self-designed general route, and years four and five include a master's seminar and specialist classes. Internships are available with faculty support. Graduates work in education and health care, HR and business, social services, the justice system, NGOs, research and private practice.

name: Social and Public Policy
overview: More than twenty courses over six semesters move from the concepts and theories of social and public policy to the design, implementation and evaluation of policies, drawing on law, economics, history and culture. Teaching includes open lectures by visiting professors from around the world, a diploma seminar for the bachelor's thesis, and encouragement to study abroad through Erasmus+. A dual diploma with Hong Kong Polytechnic University adds a BA (Honours) in Social Policy and Social Entrepreneurship. Graduates work in policy analysis, public administration, community development, education and health, in the public and private sectors, NGOs and international organisations.

name: Undergraduate Programme in International Relations
overview: More than twenty courses over six semesters treat international relations alongside law, economics, history and culture, finishing with a diploma seminar to prepare the thesis. Teaching comes from academics at Polish and international universities, with open lectures by visiting professors, 240 hours of foreign language courses, and semesters abroad through Erasmus+ and bilateral agreements with universities in Mexico, the USA, Brazil, India and South Korea. A double degree is offered with Kyungpook National University. Graduates aim for careers in international organisations, international business, public administration (especially the foreign service and ministries) and the non-governmental sector.

name: Undergraduate Programme in Political Science
overview: Taught entirely in English over six semesters by the Faculty of Political Science and International Studies, the course combines theoretical political science that builds research skills, European integration, Poland and Central and Eastern Europe, and training in communication, negotiation and persuasion. Compulsory courses and electives let you follow your interests, and students join political science associations, present at conferences and take part in debates and lectures. The degree ends with a bachelor's thesis and a diploma examination. You graduate qualified to analyse political problems and issues.

name: Biotechnology
overview: You study cell structure and organelles, biomolecules such as sugars, lipids, proteins and nucleic acids, the transmission of genetic information, human physiology and the immune system, metabolic pathways, bioinformatics, and biotechnology applied to pharmaceuticals and agriculture. A large share of your time is spent in the laboratory running experiments, analysing results and writing reports, with internships and electives that let you steer towards your career interests. Graduates work as research scientists, industrial, medical or agricultural biotechnologists, project managers, lab technicians, clinical medical representatives, science editors and teachers, or start their own ventures.

name: Business and Administration
overview: The curriculum covers leadership, marketing, accountancy, finance, management, research methods, international economics, entrepreneurship, law, human resource management and intercultural communication. Years one and two follow a common curriculum, and in year three you choose a specialisation in Business, Finance or Governance. Graduates are prepared to manage in multinational firms, work in consulting and marketing, start a business, advise on investment and finance, or run a non-profit.

name: Chemistry
overview: The programme teaches general chemistry with an emphasis on modern methods, including chemical synthesis, physico-chemical methods for studying the structure of compounds, and physical and chemical measurement techniques. Lectures are combined with laboratory classes on modern equipment. Graduates can work in laboratories, in companies that use modern technologies, in research institutions and diagnostic laboratories, in industry and at universities.

name: Criminal Justice
overview: You study substantive criminal law, criminal procedure, criminology and forensic science, with a focus on preventing and countering crime in its social and economic context and on international aspects of criminal justice. Graduates are prepared for public security institutions such as the police and penitentiary services, support roles in the judiciary, government and local administration, private security firms, and international organisations and EU institutions.

name: Culture, Thought and Humanity
overview: The programme looks at culture through philosophy: philosophy of culture, social and political thought, cultural and philosophical anthropology, cultural psychology and sociology of culture, including concepts of the person between nature and culture and the practice of cultural criticism. It has international links, including with a centre in the United States, and teachers from different parts of the world. Graduates can work in NGOs promoting intercultural dialogue, humanitarian and refugee organisations, media, cultural institutions and PR, as critics, journalists, cultural managers or political analysts, and can continue to a master's.

name: Data and Society
overview: Classical sociology meets analytical skills: labour studies, urban sociology, migration studies, digital cultures, big data analytics, research methodology, critical theories of technology, coding basics, statistical modelling, qualitative research and data visualisation. Learning is by doing, in research workshops, analysing real datasets and designing your own studies, with training in presenting findings to policymakers, NGOs, social movements and companies. Graduates are prepared for work in policy analysis, data and research consultancy, urban development, migration and integration services, digital innovation, public administration, NGOs and international bodies, or for a master's in the social sciences.

name: English for Knowledge, Culture and Innovation
overview: You develop practical English (grammar, speaking, reading, writing and pronunciation), study linguistics and English and American literature, and learn Polish plus one more language from scratch: German, French, Spanish, Italian or Russian. In the second year you choose between Global English Cultures and Languages, on varieties of English, pragmatics and intercultural communication, and Psycho-Pedagogical Aspects of Language Acquisition, on language learning, processing and the psychology of acquisition. Experimental methods in the study of language and the mind feature in the course. Graduates have data analysis, linguistic and cultural skills, and the programme prepares for CELTA and DELTA teaching qualifications and for master's study in linguistics, literature, culture or education.

name: European Cultures
overview: Lectures and seminars draw on ancient archaeology, cultural studies, art history, the history of Poland and Europe, social psychology and cultural and classical pedagogy, looking at communication systems, symbolic structures, cultural and political history, how values are transferred and European cultural heritage. Few courses are obligatory and most are elective, so you shape your own programme. The aim is to train people who can translate between cultural codes and organise cooperation between European societies, working in HR and PR for multinational firms, public administration, cultural institutions, tourism and journalism.

name: Genetics and Experimental Biology
overview: The curriculum covers cell structure, metabolism and division, nucleic acids and the genetic code, inheritance, genetic engineering techniques such as DNA electrophoresis and PCR, virology, microbiology, plant and animal diversity, and ecology. Laboratory sessions are held in small groups with specialised equipment and modern techniques in genetic engineering, histology, cytology and physiology, with some classes online. Graduates work in pharmaceutical and food laboratories, police forensic laboratories, environmental protection, plant and animal breeding, and research institutions, or continue to a master's in natural sciences.

name: International Relations - Global Studies
overview: Globalisation is studied as an autonomous process shaping all national and international actors, through economics, international relations, political science, anthropology, sociology, area studies and cultural and ethnic studies, with some input from earth sciences and physics. The course mixes obligatory courses, specialty courses and optional seminars, plus Polish language, a second foreign language and physical education, and ends with a bachelor's thesis under a professor's supervision or a bachelor's examination. International student exchange is possible.

name: International and European Environmental Law
overview: The programme gives a legal education centred on the protection and use of the environment, covering all the basic legal disciplines and treating international environmental problems holistically, including human rights and sustainable development. It aims to train specialists and entrepreneurs in environmental law. Graduates may work in international and European organisations, environmental departments of companies, specialist environmental firms and institutions, NGOs for nature protection, or as self-employed professionals.

name: Political Science
overview: The course covers political doctrines and institutions, contemporary political processes, politics and the media, political marketing and research methods, policy analysis, media content analysis, public speaking and strategic communication. Teaching includes international exchanges and research projects involving government institutions, media organisations and international companies, alongside international students and practitioners. In year three you choose Media and Politics, Comparative Politics, Global Security or Europe in the World. Graduates work as political advisers, campaign managers and policy consultants, in news, PR and political communication, in government, think tanks and international organisations, or in political consulting and public affairs firms.

name: Applied Computer Science
overview: Subjects include software development with programming languages and techniques, algorithms and data structures, computer networks, databases and data warehouses, mobile, distributed and web systems, multimedia and intelligent IT systems, IT project management, and foundations in physics and mathematics with some management and social communication. The English-taught Computer Engineering specialisation focuses on analysing and modelling complex IT systems, advanced databases and expert systems, parallel and distributed processing and AI-based methods.

name: Management
overview: You study finance and accounting, logistics and production planning, marketing and sales, human resources, business law and intellectual property, mathematical and statistical methods and IT tools. Teaching leans on case studies, workshops and simulations, with team-based projects and mobile management applications. The English-taught Organizational Management specialisation covers strategy, financial management, team leadership and the effect of global trends and digital technology on organisations. Internships take place with firms such as UBS, Credit Suisse and Polish companies in finance and logistics, and graduates become managers, project managers, business analysts, consultants, HR and marketing specialists or founders, in banking, consulting, HR and manufacturing.

name: Mechanical Engineering
overview: The seven-semester course covers methods of designing devices, the properties and selection of construction materials, modern manufacturing technologies, and technical diagnostics and repair, with mechanical engineering design as the specialisation. Teaching combines laboratory work and projects and ends with a thesis project. Internships and industrial placements are offered with employers such as Bosch, Volkswagen, Toyota, Volvo, Collins Aerospace and KGHM, and around 160 student science circles run alongside. Graduates work as design engineers, process engineers, R&D engineers and operations and maintenance engineers in the vehicle, machinery and equipment sectors.

name: Medical Informatics
overview: The seven-semester engineering course is interdisciplinary and looks at biomedical applications of artificial intelligence, big data, mobile and wearable devices, and augmented and virtual reality. You carry out your own research projects and can join one of several student circles. It follows a single track with no named specialisations. Graduates are prepared to work in hospitals and clinical and outpatient units, medical device manufacturing and distribution, research institutions, IT companies and education.

name: Electronic and Computer Engineering
overview: You learn programming in C, C++, C#, Java, Python and assembly, plus embedded systems on FPGAs, design and programming of robotic systems, PLC controllers and measurement systems, analogue and digital electronic design, and the implementation of machine learning and neural network algorithms. Graduates work in electronic systems design and manufacturing, industrial automation and robotics, software development, and research and development centres, in roles such as software developer, DevOps engineer, tester, designer or electronics engineer, and can continue to a second-cycle degree taught in English.

name: Medicine
overview: The curriculum runs from morphology (clinical anatomy, histology with embryology) and the scientific basis of medicine (biophysics, molecular biology, biochemistry), through pre-clinical subjects such as genetics, microbiology, immunology and pharmacology, to behavioural sciences including medical psychology, communication and ethics, and then clinical specialties including paediatrics, surgery, obstetrics and oncology. Practical clinical classes begin in the fourth year, and a summer clerkship follows each year, amounting to 20 weeks. Graduates work in hospitals and public or private health care, medical universities and research institutes, public health bodies, or go on to residency via the Polish medical licensing exam, or a PhD.

name: Dentistry
overview: The first years give a solid grounding in basic sciences, and from the third year you build practical experience, treating patients under supervision at the University Dental Center on the Banacha Campus. Teaching mixes lectures, seminars and practical classes, with four weeks of summer practical training after each year, which can be done at recognised institutions in your home country. The degree conforms to EU standards, and graduates can practise or continue at the university as scientists or teachers, with specialisations such as paediatric and conservative dentistry, periodontics, orthodontics and oral and maxillofacial surgery.
